Bethabara
beth-AB-uh-ruh
proper noun (place)
Hebrew, perhaps "house of the ford"; the place beyond Jordan where John baptized and pointed to Jesus as the Lamb of God.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Bethabara (called in some texts Bethany beyond Jordan) was the place east of the Jordan where John the Baptist was baptizing when he bore witness to Jesus. "These things were done in Bethabara beyond Jordan, where John was baptizing" (John 1:28). There, the day after his testimony to the priests and Levites, John saw Jesus coming and cried the great words of his witness: "Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world" (John 1:29). There he testified that he had seen the Spirit descending like a dove and remaining on Jesus, and declared, "this is the Son of God" (John 1:34). It was from Bethabara that the first disciples — Andrew, and then Peter — began to follow Jesus. Later, when the Jews sought to stone Him, Jesus withdrew again to this place beyond Jordan where John first baptized, and there "many believed on him" (John 10:40-42). Bethabara stands in the dictionary as the place where the Lamb of God was proclaimed, the spot from which the Baptist pointed away from himself to Christ, where the first disciples were drawn to the Savior, and to which the people came in faith, a witness that the whole purpose of the forerunner, and of every faithful witness, is to point men to the Lamb who bears away the sin of the world.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The place beyond Jordan where John baptized (John 1:28) and proclaimed Jesus, "Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world" (John 1:29); where the first disciples began to follow Christ.

BETHABARA, proper noun. "House of the ford"; a place beyond Jordan where John baptized.

Where John bore witness to Jesus (John 1:28).

Where he cried, "Behold the Lamb of God" (John 1:29).

Where the first disciples began to follow Jesus.

Where Jesus later withdrew and many believed (John 10:40-42).

📖 Key Scripture

John 1:28 — "These things were done in Bethabara beyond Jordan, where John was baptizing."

John 1:29 — "The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world."

John 1:34 — "And I saw, and bare record that this is the Son of God."

John 10:41 — "And many resorted unto him, and said, John did no miracle: but all things that John spake of this man were true."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Bethabara needs no defense from redefinition; its lesson is that the whole purpose of the witness is to point men away from himself to the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.

expand to see more

Self-promotion correction. The temptation of every gifted servant is to gather a following to himself. John, at the height of his fame, pointed away from himself: "Behold the Lamb of God." The dictionary holds the pattern of the faithful witness: he decreases that Christ may increase, he directs all eyes to the Savior, and he counts his ministry fulfilled not when men follow him but when they follow the Lamb. The forerunner's glory was to be the voice, not the Word.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the substitutionary heart of the gospel proclaimed at Bethabara. John named Jesus "the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world" — the sacrificial Lamb who bears the sin of His people in their place. The dictionary commends this gospel: Christ is the true Passover Lamb, the fulfillment of all the offerings, who takes away sin not by example or teaching alone but by bearing it Himself, and to Him every faithful witness must point the lost.
